title: Rhubarb Cordial
subtitle: Sharp, vivid pink, and unmistakably spring, a short-season treat
excerpt: Rhubarb cordial is made by simmering forced rhubarb with sugar and water, then straining. Vivid rose-pink colour and a distinctly tart, floral flavour. Makes about 1.5 litres.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Forced rhubarb (from Yorkshire forcing sheds) gives a vivid pink colour and sweeter flavour than field rhubarb. The colour is the whole point of this cordial.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in ice cube trays for up to 12 months.

content.text: Rhubarb cordial is best made with forced rhubarb,  the pale pink stems from Yorkshire forcing sheds that appear from January to March give a vivid, rose-pink colour that field rhubarb can't match. The flavour is distinctly tart and floral: very much its own thing. Excellent diluted with sparkling water, or used in cocktails. Makes about 1.5 litres.

items.prepNote: forced rhubarb for best colour, cut into 3 cm lengths
peeled, sliced thinly, pairs well with rhubarb

content.text: Put the rhubarb, water, and ginger if using into a large saucepan. Bring to a simmer and cook gently for 10 to 12 minutes until the rhubarb collapses completely and releases its juice. Don't stir more than necessary,  breaking the rhubarb too vigorously makes the cordial cloudier.

Pour through a fine sieve lined with muslin set over a large bowl. Do not push the pulp through,  just let it drain naturally for a clearer cordial. This takes about 30 minutes. Pushing the pulp makes it cloudy and dulls the colour. Discard the pulp.

Return the strained juice to the cleaned pan. Add the sugar and lemon juice and stir over very gentle heat until the sugar dissolves. Do not reduce,  the colour degrades with extended heat. Pour into hot sterilised bottles and seal immediately.

items.cause: Field rhubarb used instead of forced, or overcooked.
items.fix: Forced rhubarb (the bright pink kind from January to March) is essential for the vivid colour. Don't cook beyond the 12-minute mark.

items.cause: Pulp pressed through the sieve during straining.
items.fix: Let the juice drain through muslin by gravity alone, don't press. Aesthetic only; does not affect flavour.

items.cause: Rhubarb acidity varies, some batches are sharper.
items.fix: Increase sugar to 900 g or reduce lemon juice. Taste the strained juice before adding sugar and adjust.

items.cause: Very short shelf life of fruit cordials without citric acid.
items.fix: Refrigerate immediately and use within 2 weeks. Add 10 g of citric acid with the sugar for extended shelf life.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 2 to 3 weeks. Freeze for up to 12 months.
